reports.title: OceanaGold CorporationCondensed Interim Consolidated Statements of Financial Position(in millions of United States dollars, except per share data - unaudited)

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: The Company remains on track to achieve around the midpoint of its consolidated 2026 production Guidance. Production is expected to increase in the fourth quarter and be the strongest quarter of the year, primarily driven by Haile.

With Haile expecting its strongest production quarter of the year in the fourth quarter and 27,400 ounces produced in October, Haile’s production is expected to be towards the low end of its 2026 production Guidance range. At Haile, a modified mine plan was implemented in the third quarter to de-risk the Ledbetter Pit South Wall. As a result, mining activities remained focused on the lower-grade upper benches of the Ledbetter open pit during the third quarter, temporarily impacting access to higher-grade ore. By the end of September, mining had successfully advanced into the lower benches, positioning Haile to access higher-grade ore and deliver an expected increase in production in the fourth quarter.

At Macraes, production is expected to be lower in the fourth quarter, as per plan, with full-year production expected to be near the top end of its Guidance range. Production at Waihi is expected to remain relatively consistent with the third quarter, while production at Didipio is expected to be higher in the fourth quarter, driven by increased underground mining rates.

Consolidated AISC† is anticipated to be towards the upper end of the Company’s 2026 Guidance range, reflecting inflationary impacts on labour cost and operating consumables, continued investment in maintenance and reliability improvements, the component of unhedged energy costs and lower silver by-product credits, as well as the lower sales volumes expected from Haile. Fourth quarter consolidated AISC† is expected to be lower than the third quarter, underpinned by increased production at Haile. Full year AISC† at each of Macraes, Waihi and Didipio is expected to be within their respective 2026 Guidance ranges, while Haile’s AISC† is anticipated to be around the high end of its 2026 Guidance range, reflecting lower volumes, increased investment in maintenance and reliability, and broader cost inflation, including labour.

Total capital investment for 2026 is expected to be approximately $45 million, or 7%, above the Company’s total capital investment Guidance of $645 million, reflecting increased investment in growth and exploration capital. Expected higher growth capital reflects accelerated investment to support the Macraes Phase 4 (“MP4”) Project, higher investment in the mining fleet at Didipio and additional spend at the Waihi North Project due to the acceleration of certain activities previously planned for 2027. Exploration capital is expected to be approximately $10 million above its Guidance of $60 million due to expanded, success-driven drilling programs at all four sites.

desk.headline: Revenue up 46% to $655m, adjusted EPS $0.94 vs $0.40; production on track for 2026 midpoint, costs and capex at the high end
results: Revenue rose to $655m on a gold price of $4,249/oz (was $3,476) and higher sales of 140,900 oz (was 116,200).
Haile output rose 82% from a year earlier to 54,600 oz, and Macraes rose 13%. Group output was 4% lower than in Q2.
AISC fell to $1,874/oz, 13% below Q2, on lower sustaining capital and higher Didipio by-product credits.
Net profit to shareholders was $198m. Operating cash flow was $325m, and cash rose to $729m with no debt.
$79m went back to shareholders ($59m buybacks, $20m dividends). A further $0.09 dividend was declared, and the Ausgold takeover is due to close in December 2026.

guidance.summary: OceanaGold kept its 2026 ranges and says production is on track for about the midpoint, with Q4 the strongest quarter. Haile is heading for the low end, costs for the upper end, and total capital is expected about $45m (7%) above the $645m guide.

watch: Whether Haile delivers its stronger Q4 from the higher-grade lower benches of the Ledbetter pit (27,400 oz produced in October)
Cost and capital pressure: AISC at the upper end of guidance and capital spending above plan
Closing of the Ausgold (Katanning, Western Australia) deal in December and progress at Waihi North
